book.title: Supercharge
book.author: David Norman
book.subtitle: Making Operating Systems Stick Through Community-Enhanced Leadership
book.description: Supercharge is a practical leadership and operations playbook for founders, operators, and consultants using EOS/Traction or Scaling Up who find that execution systems alone produce compliance rather than commitment. The book argues that durable performance comes from pairing rigorous operating rhythms, metrics, and accountability tools with deliberate community-building practices such as truth-telling, participation, and shared ownership. It provides audits, scripts, checklists, and side-by-side framework guidance designed to make operating systems culturally sustainable rather than mechanically installed.

audienceMatch.title: Primary Audience Alignment
audienceMatch.keyCharacteristics: SMB founders, CEOs, COOs, leadership teams, and implementation-minded consultants who already use or are evaluating EOS/Traction or Scaling Up; readers who value practical frameworks, meeting cadence, scorecards, and accountability, but who recognise culture, fear, and silence as the real blockers to execution.

analysisOverview.title: Analytical Scope
analysisOverview.readership: English-speaking business and leadership readers, primarily aged 30–55, with high engagement in nonfiction focused on execution, leadership behaviour, and organisational effectiveness.
analysisOverview.classification: Business nonfiction positioned at the intersection of operating systems, leadership behaviour change, and workplace culture.
analysisOverview.personas: Centred on two core personas: the scaling operator (COO/integrator) responsible for making systems work in practice, and the executive coach or implementer tasked with making those systems stick beyond initial rollout.
analysisOverview.marketingGuidance: Positioned as the missing implementation layer for EOS/Traction and Scaling Up adopters, with strongest traction via LinkedIn, podcasts, consultant networks, leadership offsites, and bulk/team purchases.

nonFictionAdaptation.expectedReaderOutcome: Readers gain the ability to run clearer, shorter, more honest meetings; build intrinsic accountability; surface hidden issues safely; and sustain execution discipline without reverting to command-and-control dynamics.

positioning.title: Positioning
positioning.subtitle: A leadership-and-operations playbook that adds the missing relational layer to operating-system implementations
positioning.description: Supercharge sits at the intersection of practical business operating systems (Traction/EOS and Scaling Up) and human-centered leadership/culture change. It targets leaders who have already adopted—or are about to adopt—execution frameworks but feel the implementation is becoming mechanical, compliance-driven, or short-lived. The book positions itself as a durable transformation guide: it keeps the rigor of scorecards, meeting rhythms, and accountability tools while arguing that results depend on community-building practices (shared “source of truth,” belonging, truth-telling, and intrinsic accountability). This makes it especially relevant for SMB founders/CEOs, leadership teams, and the consultant/coach ecosystem supporting operating-system rollouts, offering a pragmatic bridge between operational discipline and the conversational/relational container needed for sustained behavior change.

moodAndTone.title: Mood & Tone
moodAndTone.subtitle: Earnest, coaching-forward, and systems-oriented—candid about pressure, hopeful about possibility
moodAndTone.description: The mood is pragmatic and pressurized (boardroom cadence, the weight of targets, the fear of failed change) yet consistently aspirational and restorative: the reader is challenged to relinquish control habits and move from defensiveness to openness. The tone is instructional and consultative, with a direct-address coaching voice that uses frameworks, audits, checklists, and contrast tables to create clarity and momentum. It balances urgency (“one decision away from oblivion,” data-as-truth) with a humane emphasis on belonging, courageous conversation, psychological safety, and commitment over compliance. Overall, the reading experience aims to motivate and steady overwhelmed leaders by pairing operational rigor with relational practices that reduce cynicism and make accountability feel shared rather than imposed.

opportunities.opportunity: A practical bridge between operating-system mechanics and culture change that is implementation-native (scripts, rituals, audits) rather than purely inspirational.
opportunities.rationale: Many business books either teach execution systems (EOS/Scaling Up) or discuss leadership/culture in broad terms; fewer integrate both with step-by-step practices that address why rollouts become compliance-driven and fail to transform behavior.
opportunities.potentialImpact: Positions the book as a ‘missing manual’ for sustaining operating-system adoption, increasing word-of-mouth among leadership teams and consultants who see repeated implementation fatigue.

opportunities.opportunity: Reframing accountability as intrinsic and community-supported, not enforced—while still maintaining rigorous metrics and cadence.
opportunities.rationale: Leaders often swing between rigid scorekeeping and culture-first “softness.” The manuscript explicitly argues for rigor plus belonging, offering a differentiated middle path that matches current appetite for humane, high-performance workplaces.
opportunities.potentialImpact: Expands appeal beyond strict EOS devotees to leaders who want performance without toxic control dynamics, supporting broader corporate L&D and executive-coaching adoption.

opportunities.opportunity: Decision and transition guidance for teams choosing between Traction/EOS and Scaling Up—and for organizations that already ‘installed’ a system but didn’t get transformation.
opportunities.rationale: The market includes many partial adopters and re-implementations; buyers need diagnosis and a path forward more than another framework pitch.
opportunities.potentialImpact: Captures the sizable re-implementation and consultant-led remediation segment, increasing bulk-sale potential for workshops and coaching engagements.

personas.name: Aisha Patel
personas.description: A growth-minded COO at a scaling SMB who already runs on EOS/Traction-style rhythms but feels the culture is slipping into compliance, burnout, and masked honesty. She wants a pragmatic, tool-friendly way to build psychological safety, shared ownership, and a trustworthy “source of truth” without losing operational rigor.

demographics.lifestyle: High-responsibility professional with a structured calendar; values health routines, family time, and efficient learning; frequently traveling for offsites and leadership meetings

personas.coreNeeds: A clear, repeatable playbook that upgrades leadership meetings, accountability, and cross-functional execution while reducing fear-based control. She needs language and rituals that help leaders surface what the organization is “pretending not to know,” align on metrics, and create belonging without sacrificing performance.
personas.fears: That the operating system becomes a mechanical install—short-term gains but no transformation; that meetings turn into scorecard policing; that candor disappears behind “careful masks,” leading to hidden issues, attrition, and execution drift; that she’ll be blamed for cultural problems she can’t fix alone.
personas.values: Integrity with data (no alternative facts), fairness, humane performance standards, curiosity, transparency, shared ownership, and continuous improvement.
personas.psychologicalMotivations: High need for competence and mastery; seeks control through clarity and cadence but is actively trying to replace command-and-control reflexes with facilitation and trust. Motivated by intrinsic accountability—wanting teams to commit because they belong, not because they fear consequences.

marketing.title: SUPERCHARGE Launch Plan: Make Operating Systems Stick Through Community-Enhanced Leadership
marketing.subtitle: A stage-1, authority-building marketing strategy for a practical leadership + operations book that bridges EOS/Traction and Scaling Up with belonging, truth-telling, and intrinsic accountability
marketing.objective: Position Supercharge as the go-to “missing piece” for leaders and implementers using EOS/Traction or Scaling Up by driving qualified awareness, email list growth, and pre-order/launch-week sales that convert into consulting/coaching/speaking inbound.
marketing.keyInsight: The market is saturated with operating-system “installation” advice; what leaders fear (failed adoption, disengagement, silos, and performative compliance) is actually a community deficit—readers want a practical way to pair metrics/meeting rhythms with participation, belonging, and a shared source of truth to create durable accountability.
howToUse: Use this plan in three phases: (1) authority + list-building, (2) pre-order conversion, (3) launch amplification and enterprise/consulting pipeline.
Treat EOS/Traction and Scaling Up communities as primary distribution ecosystems: podcasts, implementer networks, coach communities, and LinkedIn.
Lead with the “tools aren’t enough” contrarian hook; then immediately offer practical artifacts (audit/checklist/scripts) to prove usefulness.
Create one flagship lead magnet (Community-Enhanced Operating System Audit) and repurpose it into weekly LinkedIn posts, short videos, and podcast talking points.
Prioritize credibility: testimonials, case-style before/after stories (shorter meetings, less rehashing, clearer accountability), and comparison charts.
Instrument everything with pixel + UTM tracking; optimize creative around the highest-intent audiences (EOS/Scaling Up users; leadership/offsite buyers; consultants).
primaryKPIs: Email list growth (new subscribers/week) and lead magnet conversion rate
Cost per lead (CPL) by audience segment (leaders vs consultants)
Podcast bookings secured and average listens/downloads per appearance
LinkedIn follower growth and engagement rate (saves, comments, shares)
Pre-order volume and pre-order conversion rate from email and ads
Amazon/retailer page conversion rate and rank movement during launch window
Event/workshop inquiries and booked discovery calls (consulting pipeline)
Review velocity (number of reviews in first 30/60 days) and average rating

funnels.name: Awareness
funnels.description: Build reach and authority by challenging the ‘install the system and you’re done’ myth and naming the hidden costs below the iceberg (silos, disengagement, rework, meeting bloat). Drive to a simple landing page and lead magnet.
funnels.formats: LinkedIn thought-leadership posts and newsletters, short-form video (30–60s), podcast interviews, guest articles, carousel posts (frameworks), quote cards, PR pitches to business outlets
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for video views, landing page views, and engaged clicks; A/B test hooks (iceberg vs compliance/commitment vs source of truth). Retarget viewers and site visitors into Consideration.

funnels.name: Consideration
funnels.description: Convert attention into trust and identifiable demand using practical proof: audits, checklists, comparison charts (Traction vs Scaling Up vs Community-Enhanced overlay), and a 45–60 minute webinar/masterclass.
funnels.formats: Lead magnet (PDF + score), 3-email nurture sequence, webinar/masterclass, LinkedIn Live, case-study posts, podcast ‘bonus downloads’, retargeting ads, partner email swaps with implementers/coaches
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for email sign-ups, webinar registrations, and time-on-page. Segment email by role (CEO/COO/HR/consultant). Use retargeting with proof points (testimonial snippets, meeting-time savings, accountability outcomes).

funnels.name: Conversion
funnels.description: Drive pre-orders, bulk/team purchases, and speaking/workshop bookings using urgency (launch bonuses), clear outcomes (shorter meetings, intrinsic accountability), and concrete next steps.
funnels.formats: Pre-order campaign (bonuses: templates + video training), launch team/review crew, retailer-optimized book page copy, email sales sequence, LinkedIn pinned post + featured section, Amazon Ads, bulk/b2b outreach (HR/L&D/COOs), partner webinars with implementers
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for purchase conversions and booked calls. Use offer tiers (individual, team pack, enterprise workshop). Retarget cart/checkout intent audiences; rotate creative by segment (leaders vs consultants).

budgetAllocation.title: Budget Allocation (Guideline % Split)
budgetAllocation.breakdown: Awareness 35% (LinkedIn/video/podcast amplification + PR support), Consideration 40% (lead magnet, webinar production, retargeting, partner co-marketing), Conversion 25% (Amazon Ads, Meta retargeting, bulk outreach tooling, review/launch operations). If budget is limited: keep Awareness to organic LinkedIn + podcasts; concentrate paid spend on retargeting and Amazon high-intent keywords.

flightSchedule.title: Flight Schedule (Stage 1: 12-Week Launch Runway)
flightSchedule.timeline: Weeks 1–4: Foundation—landing page, lead magnet, pixel/UTMs, 12-post content bank, podcast pitch list, partner outreach. Weeks 5–8: Build—weekly LinkedIn newsletter + 3 posts/week, 1 webinar, retargeting begins, secure 6–10 podcast recordings. Weeks 9–10: Pre-order push—bonuses announced, 7–10 day email sprint, partner webinars, bulk outreach to implementers/coach networks. Weeks 11–12: Launch—daily LinkedIn activity, podcast drops, Amazon + retargeting spend increases, review drive, live Q&A, bulk/team promotions for leadership teams and offsites.

lookaalikeAudiences.refreshCadence: Refresh seeds every 14–30 days during active campaigns; rebuild purchaser and subscriber seeds monthly.
prioritisationRules: Prioritize value-based seeds (purchasers, booked calls) over volume seeds (video viewers).
Separate lookalikes by segment: Leaders (CEO/COO) vs Consultants/Coaches; run distinct messaging and offers.
Only scale a lookalike when CPL and downstream conversion (webinar attend rate or purchase rate) meet targets for 7 consecutive days.
Cap frequency on retargeting; rotate creative weekly during launch window.

messagingFramework.title: Messaging Framework: From Compliance to Commitment
supportingMessages: Installing EOS/Traction or Scaling Up is only the beginning; lasting change requires the relational container that makes the tools stick.
Build a shared source of truth—no politics, no alternative facts—so teams can act with clarity and speed.
Replace command-and-control with participation: rituals and conversations that create belonging and intrinsic accountability.
Stop measuring success as the absence of problems; build the conditions for possibility, learning, and extraordinary results.
Turn meetings into leadership tools, not bludgeons—shorter, clearer, and more human.
keyThemes: Community and belonging at work as performance infrastructure
Source of truth (scorecards, metrics, visible commitments)

sampleCopy.title: Sample Promotional Copy (Blurb, Posts, Email, CTA, Video)
sampleCopy.backCoverBlurb:
You can install Traction/EOS or Scaling Up and still fail to transform your company.

Supercharge offers a new playbook for leaders who want operating-system rigor without turning people into data points. David Norman argues that tools and rhythms only work when they’re paired with deliberate community-building practices—shared sources of truth, participation, and courageous conversations that convert compliance into commitment.

With practical audits, checklists, scripts, and side-by-side framework guidance, Supercharge helps leadership teams surface what they’re pretending not to know, shorten and strengthen meetings, build intrinsic accountability, and create a culture where execution and belonging reinforce each other.

Because installing the system isn’t the finish line. It’s the beginning.

socialMediaPosts.text:
Most leadership teams see only a small fraction of what’s really happening in their organization.

If you’re “installing” EOS/Traction or Scaling Up and still feeling stuck, it’s not because the tools are broken.
It’s because community is missing.

Tools + rhythms + a shared source of truth + courageous conversation = transformation.

Want the audit checklist? Comment “AUDIT” and I’ll share it.

Hard truth: a scorecard can create compliance… or commitment.

The difference is whether your operating system is paired with real participation, belonging, and ownership.

Ask your team this week:
Are our tools producing compliance—or commitment?

“Success becomes defined as the absence of problems rather than the presence of possibility.”

If your meetings are efficient but lifeless, you might have installed the system—without achieving transformation.

Supercharge is about making the system *stick* by building the community that supports it.

Processes should be a leadership tool—not a bludgeon.

If your team dreads the rhythm, you’re paying the hidden iceberg costs: rework, silence, and performative agreement.

There’s a better way: rigor + belonging + truth-telling.

videoCreativeScripts.script:
ON CAMERA (direct-to-camera, 45–60s)

“Have you ever installed an operating system—EOS/Traction or Scaling Up—and thought: ‘We’re doing the meetings, we have the scorecard… so why does it still feel like we’re not transforming?’

Here’s the problem: tools create structure, but they don’t automatically create community.

If your system produces compliance—people nodding, updating numbers, avoiding the hard truths—you’ll get activity without ownership.

Transformation happens when you pair the rhythms with a shared source of truth *and* the conversations that build belonging, participation, and intrinsic accountability.

If you want a practical way to assess this, I created a simple audit checklist. Grab it at the link.”

Clean lighting, neutral background with subtle leadership visuals (whiteboard, calendar, dashboard). The speaker addresses the camera with calm authority. Overlay kinetic text for key phrases: 'Tools aren’t enough', 'Compliance vs Commitment', 'Shared Source of Truth', 'Community is the multiplier'. Cutaways show quick b-roll: leadership team meeting, hands placing sticky notes on a board, a dashboard/scorecard on a laptop, a circle of chairs suggesting dialogue. Corporate, premium, human-centered tone.

So are the real costs of a tool-only implementation: silence in meetings, disengagement, rehashing the same issues, and leaders carrying the weight alone.

Supercharge is a new playbook that makes operating systems stick—by combining proven rhythms with community-building practices: participation, truth-telling, and a shared source of truth.

Install the system.
Build the community.
Get transformation.”
